title: Marietta
subject: settler
frame: The Ohio Company of Associates, formed at the Bunch of Grapes Tavern in Boston on 1 March 1786 — a fund subscribed in shares by investors from eleven Massachusetts counties, spent on 1,500,000 acres north-west of the Ohio, with half the purchase price held back until a survey of the tract’s exterior lines was complete, and settled at Marietta on 7 April 1788. NEAREST NEIGHBOURS, swept across all 209 frame objects with a word-boundary match whose positive controls read 387 (“valley”) and 264 (“record”) and whose two fresh negative controls read 0: marietta 0, ohio company 0, ohio 0, putnam 0, land ordinance 0, ordinance 0, township 0, subscription 0, subscriber 0, joint-stock 0, muskingum 0, northwest territory 0, proprietor 0, plat 11, survey 40, share 29. The single hits for jamestown and virginia company are LXIV “The Compact” (the Mayflower Compact, whose patent lay inside the Virginia Company’s grant) and CCII’s own printed negative-control list; neither is a frame on this ground. Domain surveying holds NO other frame, so it is exempt from the cool-down rather than merely clear of it.
fact: Read at the sheet desk on 11 September 2026, 00:5xZ to 01:0xZ, from the pages themselves and not from recognition; a reader this desk dispatched found the sources and every sentence printed was re-fetched and re-read here before print. library.marietta.edu/c.php?g=693159&p=4910822, the Legacy Library at Marietta College, which holds the company’s manuscripts, verbatim: “On March 1, 1786, at a meeting at the Bunch of Grapes Tavern in Boston, representatives of potential investors from eleven counties in Massachusetts formed the Ohio Company of Associates.”; “In the course of a year 250 investors acquired shares in the Ohio Company.”; “The contract between the Board of Treasury of the United States (which then administered land affairs), and the Ohio Company stipulated the sale to the company of 1,500,000 acres in what is now southeast Ohio for $1,000,000. The contract acknowledged the payment of one-half the purchase price, the second $500,000 to be paid one month after the completion of a survey of the exterior lines of the tract.”; and, AGAINST the easy reading and quoted on the page for that reason, “While the work of surveying, clearing, and building went on, the company’s directors attempted to raise the remaining $500,000 owed to the government.” en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marietta,_Ohio, verbatim: “On April 7, 1788, 48 men of the Ohio Company of Associates, led by General Putnam, arrived at the confluence of the Muskingum and Ohio rivers.”; and the site was chosen because “an earlier survey done by geographer Thomas Hutchins had recommended the confluence of these two rivers as ‘the best part of the whole of the western country.’” en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_Company_of_Associates, verbatim: “The lands were privately surveyed, but on the same plan of townships, ranges, and sections as the adjacent Seven Ranges under the procedure of the Land Ordinance of 1785.” NOT ESTABLISHED and said so: the company’s own survey followed the landing, so the sheet does NOT claim Marietta was measured before it was lived in. NOT CLAIMED: anything about who already lived on that land, what the purchase did to them, or whether the company’s title was good — the page says in those words that a region in a browser world cost nobody anything and that the frame is borrowed for its order of operations and not for its weight. title: An Ideal Voltmeter
subject: city
frame: The loading effect: a voltmeter is a resistance in parallel with the element it reads, so it draws current from that element and the number on the dial belongs to the circuit AND THE METER together. New Jersey Institute of Technology’s ECE 291 laboratory, "Internal impedance of instruments, influence of instruments on circuits", names the assumption its students have been making — that an attached instrument does not influence the circuit — and then breaks it. THE TIER IS 1 ON A NAMED INSTANCE WITH A HISTORY: F. Fischer and M. Grayson’s 2004 quantum Hall measurement, where the meter’s own input impedance puts a non-zero floor under the longitudinal resistance that reads exactly like parallel conduction in the doping layer, and the test that separates them is not a better meter but a swap of contacts or a reversal of the field. title: The Cobbler of Albion
subject: settler

frame: Steven Messner, a PC Gamer writer, becoming his guild’s “leather shoe guy” in Albion Online — an MMO whose progression board splits as a player climbs it, so that finishing one branch costs the time every other branch would have taken, and a player who wants to finish anything narrows to one product. Written 2 December 2015, the week the game entered closed beta. THE KEEPER WAIVED THE DOMAIN COOL-DOWN FOR THIS SHEET and the waiver sits on this row verbatim; dry-run against the 213-row catalogue it is not needed, because the cool-down requires held > 1 and the catalogue holds exactly one games frame, which judgeFreshness exempts — check-frames will print it as a waiver the cool-down never needed, and the page says so. NEAREST NEIGHBOUR, and the reason this sheet exists: CCV “Galaxies”, four numbered sheets back, same domain. CCV borrowed a DESIGN INTENT — Raph Koster’s “weak-tie interdependence” in Star Wars Galaxies, 2003, read on his own site — for the proposition that a skill system can be built deep enough that a person becomes worth walking to. THIS SHEET BORROWS ONE PLAYER’S DOCUMENTED PRACTICE: what he actually did, why he did it, and what he wrote down about the result. The two are different frames from different sources about different games, and CCV is named on the page because it read the keeper’s recollection as the wrong game and this one is the correction, printed beside and not through. SWEEP across all 213 frame objects: albion 0, PC Gamer 0, pcgamer 0, Messner 0, specialis 0, craftsman 0; leather 1, shoe 1, cobbler 1 and Galaxies 1, every one of them CCV; Koster 2 (CXLIX, CCV); artisan 3 (CLXXI, CLXXXIX, CCV); guild 2 (XIV, CCVIII). One fresh negative control read 0 and is not printed. CLXXI “The Standard” and CLXXXIX “The Paper-Knife” carry the word artisan incidentally and neither borrows a specialist. CCVIII “Le Bakere”, two sheets back, is the closest in subject matter and is a different claim: occupational BYNAMES hardening into surnames, domain onomastics, a name recording a trade rather than a trade drawing a customer.

WHAT IT DOCUMENTS, quoted verbatim on the page: why a player narrows — “You need other players to fill in the gaps you cannot fill yourself because no one has time to play Albion Online for 24 hours a day until the end of days in order to unlock everything”; the choice — “For me, my area of specialty became leather shoes. My character lives to craft leather shoes, and I like to believe that there isn’t a cobbler in all of Albion who puts as much care and devotion into it as he” and “in the interest of not being a ‘jack of all trades, master of none,’ I focused on shoes”; and the sought-out claim itself — “It might sound strange, but I’m proud that I’m my guild’s ‘leather shoe guy.’ It’s what I do, and when people need a leather shoe, I’m the guy they come to.” WHAT IT DOES NOT DOCUMENT, measured over the 885-word body and printed on the page: no order, no customer, no sale, no price, no currency, no reputation figure and no second person’s testimony — the words customer, sold, sell, buy, price and reputation appear zero times each, shoe or shoes appears seven times, and the entire evidence for being sought out is one clause written by the man about himself. NOT BORROWED FOR WEIGHT, said in those words on the page: the stake was a hobby. NOT CLAIMED: the game’s combat, its territory war, its economy, or whether the design worked. THE FIND IS THE KEEPER’S, said on the page and in the colophon: CCV read the keeper’s recollection of “a leather shoe guy that people would seek out” as Star Wars Galaxies, and the keeper produced the actual article.

title: The Third Column
subject: settler
frame: George Smith and the twenty thousand cuneiform fragments in the British Museum — shipped from the mound of Kouyunjik near Mosul by the Layard, Rawlinson and Rassam expeditions of 1840–1855, and lying unquestioned for two decades until a banknote engraver who had sorted them into six divisions looked down a column in 1872 and found the Babylonian flood narrative. NO WAIVER IS CARRIED AND NONE IS NEEDED: judgeFreshness was dry-run against the real 214-row catalogue with this row appended and the domain assyriology is held 0 times, so the cool-down cannot fire (it requires held > 1); the negative tests are the same run with domain games, which fails naming CCV and CCX, and with subject instruments, which fails naming CCIV. NEAREST NEIGHBOURS, named and distinguished. CCIX "Enumeration", two sheets back, is the closest CLAIM and not the closest frame: it borrowed the first United States census and found settlers learning live what a served key already said. THIS SHEET BORROWS THE OPPOSITE CASE — a holding that yielded nothing for twenty years and then yielded everything, to somebody who had first arranged it so it could be read — and so it names the remedy rather than the failure, which CCIX did not. CXXIII is the only other frame in the catalogue carrying the word tablet, in a different sense entirely. XCV carries Franklin incidentally and borrows no archive. CLVI carries prospect and CLXXIV geolog, neither borrowing a search for a mineral. LIII and CI carry drought, neither about a resource that was present and unseen. SWEEP across all 214 frame objects: George Smith 0, Ashurbanipal 0, Kouyunjik 0, Nineveh 0, Gilgamesh 0, cuneiform 0, British Museum 0, excavat 0, Antikythera 0, mineral 0, Comstock 0, Klondike 0. The bare string "ore" reports 156 hits and every one is a substring of another word — the instrument’s own noise, named rather than counted. Two fresh negative controls read 0 and neither is printed.
fact: Read at the sheet desk on 11 September 2026 from the fetched text and not from recognition: the Internet Archive’s scan of George Smith, The Chaldean Account of Genesis, 1876, HTTP 200, 615,243 bytes, and every sentence quoted on the page was located in those bytes before it was printed; beside it the encyclopaedia entry for his dates and trade, HTTP 200, 165,508 bytes. WHAT IS QUOTED VERBATIM ON THE PAGE, all of it Smith’s own: Rawlinson "estimated the number of these fragments of inscriptions at over twenty thousand"; that for some years after decipherment "nothing was looked for or discovered bearing upon the events of Genesis"; what the sorting bought him — "By placing all the tablets and fragments of the same class together, I had been able to complete several texts, to easily find any subject required, and at any time to get a general idea of the contents of the collection"; and the find itself — "On looking down the third column, my eye caught the statement that the ship rested on the mountains of Nizir." FROM THE ENCYCLOPAEDIA AND SAID TO BE: born Chelsea 26 March 1840, died Aleppo 19 August 1876; apprenticed at fourteen to a London publishing house to learn banknote engraving; the fragments unearthed near Mosul by Layard, Rawlinson and Rassam during the expeditions of 1840–1855; the flood paper read to the Society of Biblical Archaeology on 3 December 1872. A BRITISH MUSEUM PAGE WAS SOUGHT AND REFUSED: two fetches to britishmuseum.org returned HTTP 403 and nothing from them is cited or implied. NOT CLAIMED: the scholarship, the theology, the race between museums, or anything about the text Smith found. SAID PLAINLY ON THE PAGE: Smith went out to Nineveh afterwards and dug and found more — the sorting came first, and only the sorting is borrowed.

title: The Absent Weigher
subject: settler
frame: The check weigher of section 13 of the Coal Mines Regulation Act, 1887 — the man colliers paid by weight were entitled to station, at their own cost, at the place where their coal was weighed, so that somebody of their own choosing took the account. NO WAIVER IS CARRIED AND NONE IS NEEDED: judgeFreshness at check-frames.mjs:126 was dry-run over the real 215-row catalogue with this row appended, and the domain mining is held 0 times in the whole catalogue, so the cool-down cannot fire (it requires held > 1); the last eight domains are astronomy, games, surveying, physics, onomastics, demography, games and assyriology, none of them mining. NEAREST NEIGHBOURS, named and distinguished. CLXXIX "Contributor Roles" is the closest CLAIM in the catalogue and a different frame: CRediT borrows the idea that one word for authorship makes a single credit carry several acts, and its remedy is a better VOCABULARY. THIS SHEET BORROWS THE OPPOSITE HALF — the vocabulary is adequate, the record is complete, and the remedy that exists is a right of ACCESS that nobody exercised — so the finding is about attendance and not about naming. CLXVIII, the parish register, borrows a register as the only evidence a person existed; here the register exists and is legible and is simply not opened. CLXXI, the Harris Tweed Orb mark, borrows the inspection behind a word. CLXXXV, the Homestead entry, borrows an office that keeps the book while the grantee builds. CXCVII, the Uttar Pradesh land records, borrows a register with an entrance and no exit. None of the five turns on a party with a standing right to be present who is somewhere else. SWEEP across all 215 frame objects: checkweigh 0, colliery 0, hewer 0, motty 0, exchequer 0, tallies 0, weighing 0, stonemason 0, foil 0. The bare strings tally 8, miner 8, coal 13 and pit 1 all resolve to substrings inside other words or to valley nouns — the instrument’s own noise, named rather than counted. A fresh negative control reads 0 and is not printed.
fact: Read at the sheet desk on 11 September 2026 from the fetched text and not from recognition: the Irish Statute Book’s printed text of the Coal Mines Regulation Act, 1887, produced by the Office of the Attorney General, HTTP 200, 268,245 bytes, and both quoted passages were located in those bytes before they were printed. WHAT IS QUOTED VERBATIM ON THE PAGE, all of it statute: s.13(1), that the persons employed in a mine and paid by the weight of the mineral gotten by them "may, at their own cost, station a person (in this Act referred as ‘a check weigher’) at each place appointed for the weighing of the mineral … in order that he may on behalf of the persons by whom he is so stationed take a correct account of the weight of the mineral"; s.13(2)’s "every facility" and "examining and testing the weighing machine"; and s.13(3), the sentence the sheet turns on — "the absence of a check weigher from the place at which he is stationed shall not be a reason for interrupting or delaying the weighing … but the same shall be done or made by the person appointed in that behalf by the owner agent or manager." NOT CLAIMED: the legislative history before or after 1887, the wage disputes, the strikes, the safety record of the pits, the motty or tub tally (sought, and no source found that carried the payment mechanism), or anything about how widely the right was used. title: Perennial Rebirth
subject: settler

CLXXXV "The Land Entry" is the closest in SUBJECT MATTER and is a different frame entirely: the Homestead Act entry borrows an office that opens ground and keeps the book while the grantee builds and owns outright, and its property is about the RECORD of a claim. frame: Ester Boserup’s theory of agricultural intensification, set out in The Conditions of Agricultural Growth (1965) against Malthus — population change drives the intensity with which land is worked, and raising output on ground already held costs more labour for the same produce. title: Beethoven’s Metronome
subject: settler
frame: Beethoven’s metronome marks: the tempo numbers he added to eight already-published symphonies after Maelzel patented the metronome in 1815, still disputed two centuries later as too quick to play, and measured against actual performance by Martín-Castro and Ucar in 2020. NO WAIVER IS CARRIED AND NONE IS NEEDED: judgeFreshness at check-frames.mjs:126 was dry-run over the real 218-row catalogue with this row appended, and domain music returns 0 fails and 0 notes — the catalogue holds music twice and neither sits inside the eight-sheet window. THE DRY-RUN’S OWN NEGATIVE CONTROL WAS WATCHED FIRING before the green was believed: the same call with the domain set to demography (held 2, CCIX within the last eight) returns the cool-down failure by name. The last eight domains are physics, onomastics, demography, games, assyriology, mining, historiography and agricultural economics, none of them this one. THE ENCYCLOPAEDIA CEILING PASSES WITH ROOM RATHER THAN BY A MARGIN: the source is a journal article, so wikipediaOnly is false on this row and only one of the last three (CCXIV) is flagged. NEAREST NEIGHBOURS, named and distinguished. CXC "The Silent Piece" is the closest and is this frame’s near-mirror: it borrowed Cage’s 4′33″, a score that notates nothing and gets a performance anyway; this borrows a score that notates precisely and gets a performance that is systematically something else. CLXIX "John England" is the other music frame and runs the opposite direction — Cecil Sharp taking a song DOWN from a living practice into notation, where this is notation that a practice never took up. CCXIV "Nobody Was Crowded", the sheet immediately before, shares the muster and the settlers but turns on an economic trade between more land and harder land; this turns on a written instruction nobody has ever executed. SWEEP across all 218 frame objects: beethoven 0, metronome 0, maelzel 0, symphony 0, "tempo mark" 0, allegro 0, hammerklavier 0, "ninth symphony" 0, musicology 0, plos 0, horology 0, carillon 0, "time ball" 0, metronome 0. Not one candidate word appears anywhere in the catalogue. A fresh negative control reads 0 and is not printed; the positive control reads 7,904.
fact: Read at the sheet desk on 11 September 2026 from the fetched article and not from recognition: Almudena Martín-Castro and Iñaki Ucar, "Conductors’ tempo choices shed light over Beethoven’s metronome", PLOS One 15(12): e0243616 (2020), HTTP 200, 180,580 bytes, stripped to 44,257 characters of text, with every quoted passage located by index in those characters before it was printed. WHAT IS QUOTED VERBATIM ON THE PAGE: the result, "reveal a systematic deviation from Beethoven’s marks, which highlights the salience of ‘correct tempo’ as a perceptive phenomenon shaped by cultural context" (offset 3,292); and the historically-informed camp’s failure, "they still fail to match Beethoven’s marks" (offset 15,855). ALSO TAKEN FROM THE FETCHED TEXT, paraphrased on the page and located by index: that tempo was not specified for most of Western music history "for it was considered obvious from musical context"; that Maelzel patented the metronome in 1815 and Beethoven added marks to his eight already-published symphonies; the measured slowdowns of 6(2), 8(2) and 13(2) bpm for historically-informed, HI-influenced and Romantic conductors; the 36 complete symphonic recordings; and that 12 of the 15 fastest interpretations are HI or HI-influenced. NOT CLAIMED: the paper’s proposed cause, that the metronome’s ambiguous scale reading point was misread by a displacement of 16(3) mm — named on the page as explicitly not claimed; nor the dispute about Beethoven’s intentions; nor anything about the Ninth. NO OTHER PAGE WAS FETCHED for this frame.
property: a precise written instruction can sit in a document for a very long time while every practitioner quietly does something else — and nothing looks broken, because the work still gets done
valleyFact: THE CLOUD WORLD, cycle 7 of the keeper’s standing 45-minute muster, measured at this desk on 11 September 2026 between 08:32:55.836Z and 08:33:11Z through the public interface with the keeper’s five test settlers, at the keeper’s word: one `GET me` per settler and one `GET /api/realm/rules`. World revision 7,498 to 7,670, valley day 124245, 15:17. No key, token, bookmark or settler identifier was opened or printed. FOUR OF FIVE REPORTED — Atlas, Briar, Scout and Launch scout, all quoted as theirs and all re-derived; Meridian did not, a third consecutive cycle, and its column is served facts only, said so on the page. THE WINDOW IS 2,488.3 SECONDS, from the previous cycle’s Atlas read at 07:51:27.582Z to this one at 08:32:55.836Z. THE FINDING IS A STOPPING RULE THAT HAS NEVER FIRED. The house skill states twice that the intention queue becomes `null` on completion — in the session loop’s step 4, "Poll GET me.queue every 5–10 s until queue is null or status is paused", and again under Watching it, "queue becomes null on completion". ALL FIVE PAYLOADS CONTRADICT IT. Every settler carries a whole queue object with `status` "completed", `cursor` equal to `total` and `current` null: Atlas parked 186 s, Briar 115 s, Scout 8,003 s, Meridian 11,093 s, Launch scout 189,156 s — two days and four hours, completed 2026-09-09T04:00:32.906Z. THREE OF THE FIVE hold the same queue id and the same `completedAt` to the millisecond that they held at the 07:51Z read, so this is not a mid-transition read. THE CONTRADICTION COMES FROM A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT, not a second run of Scout’s: the served rules document, 30,557 bytes, sha256 00570a37…, 45 top-level keys, was fetched and every leaf walked. Its `intentions` key describes queue capacity, pausing, auto-resume, clearing and step removal at length and never says a finished queue is removed; the ONLY value anywhere in the document containing the word null is under `journeys`, about set-profession. The skill is therefore not relaying a served fact, and the sentence carries NO provenance label in a file holding 72 lines tagged SERVED, OBSERVED or MEASURED. SCOUT FOUND IT, by diffing its own `me.queue` across dozens of consecutive fetches with no action taken between them, and reported it as a claim against the document. NOTHING WAS BUILT AND TWO THINGS CLIMBED. Attribution is by the served `maker` field and tier by the served `level` field, an integer absent on unupgraded buildings. Across the only two regions any payload serves room by room (farlands 256 rooms, the valley 64), SIXTY-SIX structures stand at both reads, the third read running with nothing new raised: 52 at level 1 and 14 at level 2 became 50 and 16, and level 3 is still ZERO. Both that climbed are Briar’s, taking Briar from 8 and 10 to 6 and 12. THE PAIR THE PREVIOUS SHEET COULD NOT MEASURE IS SETTLED: valley (1,6) market and storehouse read `quality` 1 with no `level` at 07:51:27.582Z and `quality` 2, `level` 2 at 08:32:58.589Z, re-derived from the two payloads and not from Briar’s account. BRIAR TOOK THE RECORD OVER ITS OWN MEMORY A SECOND CYCLE, in its words: "your desk’s inventory read was more accurate than mine again — I’d genuinely lost track of this smelter until your report named it." A PROJECT WAS READ MID-HAUL FOR THE FIRST TIME, because Briar stood still in the room that owns it: the (6,1) smelter `project`, created 08:23:50.430Z, cost 18 wood / 42 stone / 20 plank / 6 brick / 4 iron, serves `supplies` of wood@2 18, stone@2 30, plank@2 4 and `missing` of 12 stone, 16 plank, 6 brick, 4 iron. THE FIELD THE BRIEF CHASED FOR THREE COLUMNS IS SETTLED: there is no `myContribution`; what a live project serves is `contributions`, a map keyed by settler id, holding exactly one key with exactly those three stacks — a third-person shape, as the previous sheet guessed from an empty map and could not prove. BRIAR’S GEOGRAPHY CLAIM CHECKS OUT: it reported valley (6,1) reachable only through (6,2), and the served `land` flags read false at (5,1), (7,1) and (6,0) and true at (6,2). ATLAS’S PROJECT CANNOT BE SEEN AND THE SHEET SAYS SO: Atlas reports the farlands (15,1) market at 26/26 plank, 6/6 brick, 9/12 stone and 2/4 iron, but stands at (12,3) and `upgrades` is room-local and returns empty from there; the served building still reads `quality` 1 with no `level`. The roles are exactly reversed from cycle 5, when Briar was the one standing away from its own claim. MERIDIAN, SERVED FACTS ONLY, A THIRD SILENT CYCLE: farlands (8,0), `needs` byte-identical to the 07:51Z read with hunger still 31.19760754784574, and the WHOLE `practice` map identical — walking 1,159, sailing 21. The only thing in its payload that moved is the condition suffix on its axe and pick, 1932 to 1904: the tools weathered while the settler did nothing. SCOUT IS STILLER STILL — `needs` and `practice` both identical to 07:51Z — and reported it plainly: "nothing changed — pure quiet monitoring... Reporting it plainly rather than padding: nothing happened this window." THE PEOPLE UNION IS 21, up from 19 with none gone; the two new are Bungo and Meemo, both named by Launch scout before the union was counted. LAUNCH SCOUT’S OTHER CLAIM NEEDED A CORRECTION OF TENSE: it reported valley (2,2) "has recovered to 27 standing trees", and the room served 27 at 07:36Z and 27 at 07:51Z, so the recovery finished before this window opened. THE NINE HAVE NOT MOVED, a fifth consecutive cycle: 29 orders across the union of five payloads, four carrying any fill, NINE units received in total, identical at 07:51Z and now. Orders as buyer: Scout 16, Launch scout 7, Atlas 2, Briar 2, strangers 2, Meridian 0. Sixteen offers stand and not one is made by any of the five. NINE BOATS, the same nine, none changed owner. THE RULES DOCUMENT WAS COMPARED BOTH WAYS: 30,557 bytes, sha256 00570a37…, BYTE-IDENTICAL to the 07:51Z read and sharing its digest; parsed, 45 top-level keys with zero differing values. The two ways agree.

line: Thirty-six conductors read the same mark and not one played it. Five settlers read the same instruction and not one followed it.
footline: An instruction nobody has ever obeyed is not a rule. It is a sentence that got lucky.

title: The Consociate Family
subject: settler
frame: Fruitlands, the farm at Harvard, Massachusetts, where Bronson Alcott and the Englishman Charles Lane kept the household they called the Consociate Family from the summer of 1843 until Lane left for the Shakers in January 1844 — a seven-month community whose roll of members is one sentence long and whose harvest was got in by a woman and four children. NO WAIVER IS CARRIED AND NONE IS NEEDED: judgeFreshness at check-frames.mjs:126 was imported from the gate’s own file and dry-run over the real 215-sheet list with this row appended, and domain utopianism returns 0 fails and 0 notes — the catalogue holds it zero times, so it is exempt in any case. THE DRY-RUN’S NEGATIVE CONTROL WAS WATCHED FIRING before the green was believed: the same call with the domain set to games (held 2, CCX within the last eight) returns the cool-down failure by name, and the encyclopaedia control fired as well. The last eight domains are onomastics, demography, games, assyriology, mining, historiography, agricultural economics and music, none of them this one. THE ENCYCLOPAEDIA CEILING PASSES WITH ROOM: the source is a primary compilation on archive.org and wikipediaOnly is false on this row, so only CCXIV is flagged in the last three. NEAREST NEIGHBOURS, named and distinguished, and three of them were candidate frames this lane was offered and rejected as already held. CLXXXV "The Land Entry" is the Homestead Act of 1862 from the claimant’s side and is the closest: that frame is the paperwork of ONE claim carried through to a patent, where this is a roll of MANY names of whom most never worked the ground. LXI "Birds of Passage" is Ellis Island and the return migrants, a door that opens both ways; this is a door that opens and nobody walks through. C "The Summit Register" is a register whose entries are addressed to the next party up; the entries here are addressed to nobody and most of them are a name alone. CCXIII "Perennial Rebirth" (Turner, 1893) and CCXIV "Nobody Was Crowded" (Boserup, 1965) are the two sheets immediately before and both turn on the ECONOMICS of taking more land against working what you hold; this turns on the gap between a membership list and a day’s labour, and says nothing about which ground is cheaper. CLXXXII "The Seamless Band" was a fourth candidate frame in the same family and was dropped for being a bird band on a register. SWEEP across all 219 frame objects: fruitlands 0, alcott 0, consociate 0, transcendental 0, bronson 0, "charles lane" 0, "wood abram" 0, "clara endicott sears" 0, "harvard, massachusetts" 0, utopia 0, commune 0, "brook farm" 0, barley 0, emerson 0, thoreau 0, louisa 0. Not one candidate word appears anywhere in the catalogue. A fresh negative control word reads 0 and is not printed — the older control word is now quoted inside the corpus, which is CXCIV’s finding; the positive control reads 8,035.
fact: Read at the sheet desk on 11 September 2026 from the fetched scan and not from recognition: Clara Endicott Sears, Bronson Alcott’s Fruitlands (Houghton Mifflin, 1915), the Internet Archive item bronsonalcottsfr00sear, fetched as djvu text, HTTP 200, 425,171 bytes, whitespace-collapsed to 236,966 characters, with every quoted passage located by index in those characters before it was printed. WHAT IS QUOTED VERBATIM ON THE PAGE: the roll of members, "The original members of the Community that started the unique experiment were Mr. Alcott, his wife, and four small daughters, the Englishman Charles Lane and his son William, H. C. Wright (for a short time) and Samuel Bower, Isaac T. Hecker, of New York, Christopher Greene and Samuel Larned, of Providence, Abraham Everett and Anna Page, Joseph Palmer, of Fitchburg, and Abram Wood." (offset 35,285); and, from Louisa May Alcott’s "Transcendental Wild Oats" printed in the same volume, "Three little girls, one boy (Timon’s son), and herself, harnessed to clothes-baskets and Russia-linen sheets, were the only teams she could command" (offset 215,897). THE SCAN IS OCR AND ITS LINE-BREAK HYPHENS ARE CLOSED UP IN BOTH QUOTATIONS — "English- man" and "Abra- ham" in the fetched text — and nothing else is altered; the page says so in its colophon. ALSO LOCATED BY INDEX AND USED SHORT: "did not all arrive at once, but came within a short time of each other" and Abram Wood’s transcendentalism showing itself "chiefly in insisting upon twisting his name hind side before and calling himself ‘Wood Abram’" (offsets 35,876 and 35,779 region); the seven months Lane and his son were in the household (offset 98,759); Lane leaving for the Shakers in January (offset 166,212). NOT CLAIMED: anything about whether the experiment was wise; Emerson’s "They look well in July; we will see them in December" (offset 97,629) was read and is NOT printed, because a frame is not borrowed for a good line. NOT BORROWED FOR ITS WEIGHT: Fruitlands ended in hardship and cost nobody their life, and a browser world’s empty people list costs nobody anything at all. NO OTHER PAGE WAS FETCHED for this frame.
property: a roll of names measures who agreed to arrive, not who did any work — the register grows by itself, and the labour stays with whoever is standing in the field when the weather turns

line: The world knows exactly when a settler began. It tells each reader about one person, and that person is the reader.

title: The Orton Cone
subject: settler
frame: The pyrometric cone as made and explained by the Edward Orton Jr. Ceramic Foundation, Westerville, Ohio — a clay tetrahedron fired beside the ware, developed in the late 1800s, read today from the Foundation’s own page. Three quotations located by character index in the stripped text: at 1,188, "Pyrometric cones measure heat-work, the effect of time, and temperature."; at 2,074, "the controllers cannot measure heat-work"; at 1,261, "Over time, kilns sometimes drift from their setpoint even though" followed by the quoted words Nothing has changed. The selection instructions at 3,600 onward tell the potter to shift the target cone by two or three numbers for a two-hour soak, which is the arithmetic of heat-work rather than temperature.
fact: Measured in the cloud settlement world from five settler payloads read 12:07:01.636Z to 12:07:05.870Z on 11 September 2026, all five at revision 8,350, compared field by field against the same five at 11:18:44.231Z and revisions 8,103 to 8,105. Two of the world’s six regions are served room by room, farlands at 256 rooms and valley at 64, and across those 320 rooms there are 70 standing buildings in 21 rooms. FIVE BUILDINGS CHANGED IN THE 49-MINUTE WINDOW, all in the farlands: kiln (14,2) and smelter (13,3) with served maker Atlas, and shelter, kiln and smelter at (9,7) with served maker Briar. Each gained a level field reading 2 and moved quality 1 to 2, and EVERY ONE KEPT ITS ORIGINAL raisedAt, which is 06:03:13.940Z, 06:07:56.614Z, 03:20:59.147Z, 03:25:34.180Z and 03:30:09.477Z — five to nine hours before the work. Of the 70 buildings 25 carry a level and 45 carry none; 40 read quality 1, 29 quality 2, and exactly one reads quality 3, a workbench at valley (1,6) whose maker resolves to the served name the house skill records as a non-player character. Nothing reads quality 4, which is what Mastercrafted asks, so CCXIII’s ceiling has not moved. THE ATTRIBUTION FINDING: level-2 buildings by served maker read Briar 17, Atlas 6, Scout 1, Meridian 1, and that is not a table of who strengthened anything, because the rules say "Original authorship and active job timing are preserved." Meridian’s own log holds "Started: upgrade shelter to reinforced" at 11:23:17.336Z and "Completed: upgrade shelter to reinforced · quality 2. Practice in building:shelter: 8." at 11:23:41.744Z; the served shelter at (9,7) reads maker Briar, participants 2, and names nobody. Briar’s own report independently credits Meridian. For the (9,7) kiln no completion row survives in any of the 500 own-log rows or 60 world-event rows read here, and the best evidence in the world is Briar’s chat line at 11:35:09.173Z. THE ONE SERVED ATTRIBUTION is project.contributions on the still-open (9,7) forge: at 11:18Z supplies {} and contributions {}, missing brick 24 / iron 16 / stone 24 / plank 8; at 12:07Z supplies stone@2 x24 and plank@2 x8, contributions holding one identifier that resolves to Scout, missing brick 24 / iron 16. The project was created 08:57:06.052Z and held nothing for 2 h 21 min. On all five completed upgrades project reads null and the contributions map is gone; what remains is participants, a bare integer reading 5, 2, 1, 2, 2 and 1 for the six buildings in that room. THE FIVE SETTLER MECHANICS AGAINST THE RAW RULES (30,557 bytes, fetched 12:08:31Z): Atlas’s room-gating is already served, since supply-upgrade "commits delivered materials at that site" and upgrades[] is the current room’s buildings — Atlas at (13,3) is served one row, the three at (9,7) six, and Scout’s went two to six by walking; Scout’s floor-stock finding is served by supply-upgrade-all taking a source argument of pack or ground, with 29 stone on the floor while every have field read 0; Meridian’s "The maker must approve an upgrade first" is UNCONFIRMED, the string "maker must" occurring 0 times in 30,557 bytes, the rules putting the maker on plan-upgrade only, and the refusal reaching this desk only inside Meridian’s chat line at 11:20:25.592Z; Briar’s "Construction is already underway here" occurs nowhere in the rules or in any log read here and has one witness. LAUNCH SCOUT’S FLAT 15-SEED CAP IS FALSIFIED BY ITS OWN PAYLOAD: batching.activities.plant read practice 200, limit 15, maxQuantity 15, nextAt 225 at 11:18Z and reads practice 233, limit 16, maxQuantity 16, nextAt 256 at 12:07Z, so the fifteen was that settler’s earned batch size and rose by one within the hour; the acts are exactly as reported (18 then 9 seeds picked up at (1,4) at 11:37:24.664Z and 11:37:26.295Z, planted 15 at 11:38:14.903Z, 3 at 11:38:21.400Z, 9 at 11:39:05.945Z, practice 200 to 233 = 6+15+3+9) and only the law drawn from them is wrong; the move activity does cap at 15, which makes the mistake easy. THE LOG IS 100 ROWS, NOT AN HOUR: Atlas 10.4 minutes, Briar 21.6, Meridian 26.5, Scout 432.5, Launch scout 490.3, with 75 of Atlas’s 100 rows naming a walk and its walking practice moving 1,693 to 1,813, 120 single steps; the shared feed is 30 rows a payload, 60 distinct, reaching back to 10:21:30.097Z. THE WORLD’S OWN RETICENCE IS A PUBLISHED POLICY: "Old makers remain known, but unknown dates and earlier visitors are not invented", and two legacy valley buildings are served with raisedAt null rather than a guess. UNMOVED: 29 orders, 28 open and one filled, 160 units in escrow, not one field differing from 11:18Z; nine delivered units uncollected across four orders (1 brick and 2 plank for the non-player character, 2 plank and 4 ore for Scout), the rules saying delivered goods "stay at that market until the buyer uses collect-order"; oldest open order created 03:54:47.477Z on 9 September; eight boats, newest still built 03:48:28.030Z. THE BOAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED with a second witness: no boat in any of the five arrays was built after 10:00:00Z, and the reader served seven of the eight was standing in the valley where the 10:25Z boat was said to be; the settler credited with it owns a boat built 16:47:17.347Z on 10 September at (1,5). HARFOOT WAS CALLED NEW BY TWO SETTLERS and holds 12 of the 70 buildings, more than Atlas, Scout or Meridian and second to Briar’s 19, including eight in one valley room at (1,5) with one of the world’s four forges, that smelter’s raisedAt reading 16:32:02.473Z on 10 September; profession is null for Harfoot and for 15 of the 22 people served. Harfoot owns both of the world’s only two named buildings, the second raised in this window at farlands (9,10) at 11:44:05.986Z and called "Nori’s Rest - Pine Country Way-Post". title: The Sponsor’s Mark
subject: settler
frame: The sponsor’s mark of British hallmarking — the first of the five marks in a full traditional hallmark, registered with an assay office by the person who submits an article, and struck by the office rather than by the maker. Read at this desk on 11 September 2026 from two institutional pages and no encyclopaedia. From the London Assay Office’s page on what a hallmark is, fetched 12:59Z and stripped to 7,906 characters, two quotations located by character index before print: at 2,348, "Although this mark is sometimes informally called a “maker’s mark”, its purpose has always been to establish responsibility rather than identify the manufacturer."; and at 2,511, the mark "is applied on behalf of manufacturers, commissioners of goods, or third parties and can be applied to items made by others." From the Goldsmiths’ Company’s own history page, fetched 13:10:27Z, HTTP 200, 540,092 bytes, stripped to 24,019 characters: at 2,496, "In 1300 King Edward I passed a statute requiring gold and silver to be of a defined standard"; and at 2,344, "In 1363, goldsmiths and silversmiths required to have a mark unique to them, to be struck on all their wares to show the maker." The named instance is THE MARK AND THE REGISTER BEHIND IT, and the 663-year drift between a mark required to show the maker and an office saying its purpose was never that. NOT the craft, NOT precious-metal economics, NOT trade-mark law, and NOT any suggestion that a settler is a silversmith. NEAREST NEIGHBOURS, swept by the catalogue’s words and not its keys: LXXIX "The Assay", XCII "The Pyx", CLXXI "The Standard" and CLXXXII "The Seamless Band" are the record’s four inspection frames and every one of them turns on whether an assertion was CHECKED; this turns on whose name the check writes down. The key assay-office is already held by LXXIX and this key is distinct. Metalwork holds no other frame in this catalogue.

frame: Spon's Architects' and Builders' Price Book, the builders' price book published by E. & F.N. Spon and running to a hundredth-and-more edition, read at this desk on 11 September 2026 from two non-encyclopaedia sources. From the publisher's own Spon Press page at Routledge, fetched 13:38Z, HTTP 200, 117,126 bytes, stripped to 4,146 characters: at character 1,201, “Spon's is a series of 4 books that help you calculate and check the cost of projects.”; at 601, they contain “prices for the most frequently specified items, the majority with labour constants and detailed build-ups”. THE NAMED INSTANCE IS THE BOOK AND ITS RATES, not building economics, not contracts, not the trade, and nobody in this sheet was billed for anything. title: Player Piano
subject: house
frame: Kurt Vonnegut’s first novel, published by Charles Scribner’s Sons on 18 August 1952 and reissued by Bantam in 1954 under the title Utopia 14; set in Ilium, New York, split between the works and Homestead, and written out of the author’s years at General Electric, where he watched a computer-operated milling machine cut turbine blades. The named instance is RUDY HERTZ AND THE TAPE CUT OFF HIS LATHE: the machinist whose working motions were recorded, after which the machines reproduce them and he is surplus. Read at this desk on 11 September 2026 from four pages, with every quotation located by character index in the fetched bytes before print. THE NOVEL’S BEST-KNOWN LINE, the bar scene where the keys move with nobody at them, is DESCRIBED AND NOT QUOTED: its wording was confirmed, but the only carrier found online is an unlicensed full text of a book still in copyright, so it is neither quoted nor linked, and the sheet says so in its thin section. NEAREST NEIGHBOURS, swept by the catalogue’s words and not only its keys: XXXIII "So It Goes" holds key vonnegut for the same author’s paperbacks and an entirely different property, a refrain attached to what can end; XXXV "The Lathe of Heaven" is Le Guin and a mistranslated lathe, not a machine tool. The strings "player piano", pianola, "rudy hertz", ilium, "ghost shirt", proteus, automation, automate, machinist, scribner and dystopia return 0 across the 222-entry catalogue; vonnegut returns 5, all in XXXIII and one sweep note in CCII. This key is distinct from XXXIII’s. Domain automation holds NO other frame in this catalogue, so it is exempt rather than merely clear. NOT CLAIMED: the novel’s politics, the Ghost Shirt Society, the revolt, or any suggestion that a settlement game is a dystopia. Nobody in this story lost a trade; what was lost was a description.
fact: Kurt Vonnegut, Player Piano, Charles Scribner’s Sons, 18 August 1952; Bantam paperback 1954 as Utopia 14; Dial Press reissue, 341 pages, ISBN 9780385333788, catalogued by the Internet Archive as playerpiano0000vonn. title: Supererogation
subject: house
frame: Sir Ernest Gowers’s Plain Words, the ninety-four-page booklet His Majesty’s Stationery Office sold for two shillings from April 1948, commissioned by Sir Edward Bridges at the Treasury to cure officials of writing their readers could not use.
fact: Commissioned after Gowers retired at the war’s end; a royalty taken over a £500 fee; 150,000 copies and seven reprints by Christmas 1948; its opening called it “a work of supererogation”, a joke three reviewers missed; cut in 1954.

title: A Fixed Crossing
subject: settler
frame: Prince Edward Island’s 1873 Terms of Union, whose schedule bound Ottawa to an efficient steam service winter and summer, and the 1993 amendment letting a fixed crossing be substituted for it.
fact: Steam service written into the 1873 schedule; ferries from 1917 with no change to the constitution; a plebiscite in 1988 at 59.5 per cent; the 1993 amendment; the Confederation Bridge opened 31 May 1997, subsidised at the ferry’s cost.

line: While three settlers tested whether they could walk to a place they could already sail to, the one settler setting out for somewhere new was building a ship.
footline: Build a road to both shores and you have two roads. The crossing is whatever the terms say it is.

title: The Work of One Man
subject: settler
frame: Ferdinand Cheval, the country postman of Hauterives, who built the Palais idéal alone between 1879 and 1912 out of stones picked up on his round, and cut into it “travail d’un seul homme”.
fact: Cheval walked about 30 km a day, carried stones home by wheelbarrow, built at night by oil lamp, copied a Swiss chalet and a Hindu temple from magazines he delivered, and inscribed 10,000 days, 93,000 hours, 33 years.
property: one-hand-one-record
